title: kv-cache: improve memory manager and eviction heuristics for spillover/paging
author: Ayesha Patel
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and suboptimal eviction under mixed traffic (short/long sequences) was causing elevated GPU memory pressure and increased paging/spillover events. This PR revisits the memory accounting and eviction priority logic to reduce unnecessary spillover and improve throughput stability. Summary of changes: 1) introduce a per-segment allocation tracker to improve fragmentation visibility and prioritize evicting small, high-fragment segments; 2) add an adaptive spillover threshold that increases tolerance during short-sequence dominated workloads and tightens when long-sequence tail latency rises; 3) implement opportunistic compaction (defrag) triggered when fragmentation > 25% and IO/backpressure is low; 4) change eviction priority to combine recency, token footprint, and fragmentation delta (new score) instead of pure LRU; 5) integrate memory-manager signals with the request scheduler so defrag and compaction tasks are deprioritized under sustained high throughput; 6) telemetry: add fragmentation_percent, compaction_runs, spillover_events, and eviction_score histogram metrics; 7) tests and benchmarks (unit, integration, and perf harness); 8) rollout: feature-flagged, staged rollout with Canary on dedicated hosts then global. Backwards compatibility: default configuration preserves previous thresholds until rollout sets adaptive mode. Related work: ENG-1423 (KV cache memory accounting), ENG-1500 (spillover telemetry), and incident SUP-2174. Checklist: [x] design doc updated, [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] perf runs attached, [x] feature flag, [x] rollout plan. See commits and changed files for implementation details.

release_notes: Improved KV cache memory manager with fragmentation-aware eviction and adaptive spillover thresholds. Reduces unnecessary GPU spillover and improves tail latency under mixed workloads. Feature-flagged and rolled out incrementally.
review_comments: Sophie: Can we add a short-circuit to skip compaction when host memory pressure > 80%? — addressed in compaction.cc with scheduler signal
Marco: eviction score weighting needs doc and default tuning; added config and documented rationale
Ravi: observed a race when cancelling compaction during shutdown — fixed and added regression test
performance_summary: Perf harness (n=3) on dedicated canary hosts: spillover events reduced by 68%, average per-token latency improved 9% on mixed workloads, tail (p95) latency improved 22% during long-sequence bursts. Compaction CPU overhead measured ~4% when triggered; scheduler integration avoids compaction during sustained high QPS.
rollout_plan: Feature flagged; enable on 2 canary dedicated pools for 48h, monitor fragmentation_percent and spillover_events, then enable gradually across dedicated region hosts, followed by hosted API if metrics stable for 7 days.
notes: Conservative defaults keep adaptive mode off. Operators can enable via config: redwood.kv_cache.adaptive_eviction=true. Observability dashboards and alerts added under 'KV Cache / Memory' in Redwood Console.
